models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Light easterlies and near-flat seas hold through tomorrow - Panarea to Filicudi is a downwind motor-sail, depart 06:00.
briefing.synopsis: A slack, low-gradient easterly regime sits over the Aeolians with no organised system in the payload. ECMWF IFS (06 Oct 00Z) and AIFS (06 Oct 06Z) both keep wind at Panarea in the 3-9 kt band from E through SSE overnight, backing to SE then E through Saturday, with seas 0.1-1.0 ft. Through 7-8 Oct the trend is for the flow to stay light and easterly, easing further on the 8th before a WNW-NW component appears on the 9th for the Salina-Portorosa run. Nothing in the payload shows a strengthening or frontal passage inside 48 h.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: Dawn at Panarea is light: 4.4 kt from about 102° at 06:00 on the consensus, but the models disagree on that hour by more than 6 kt (range 1.0-7.4 kt), so expect anything from glass to a light breeze. Recommended departure for Panarea → Filicudi is 06:00, with 6.2 kt SE, gusts to 17.3 kt, 0.8 ft seas and a 113° TWA - broad reach, verdict go. Later slots are no worse (12:00-16:00 at 6.7 kt E, 1.0 ft, a dead run), so the early start is about arriving in daylight with reserve, not about escaping weather. Plan on engine time over the 28 nm in this little air.

passage_notes.note: Already in hand today: all windows 5-8 kt SE/ESE, seas 0.1-0.6 ft, beam to broad reach, verdict go throughout.
Go on all windows. 6-7 kt SE backing E, seas 0.8-1.0 ft, broad reach to run. Gusts to 16-17 kt are IFS interval-maxima against a 6 kt mean, reported but not treated as a caution.
Very light: 3-6 kt SSE/SE, seas 0.5-0.7 ft. Early windows close reach; by 14:00 the TWA is 20° - head to wind, motor. One IFS gust spike to 24.7 kt against a 5.6 kt mean in that afternoon slot.
Wind swings to W/NW, 5-8.5 kt, seas building slowly to 1.8 ft by the afternoon. Best sailing angle is the 08:00 window at 8.5 kt WNW, broad reach. Three days out - treat as provisional.

cautions: Model spread at 06:00 tomorrow at Panarea is 1.0-7.4 kt; the 4.4 kt figure is a mean, not a certainty. Be ready to motor the whole 28 nm.

IFS gust figures in this light air are interval maxima - the 21.6 kt gust at the San Pietro buoys and the 17 kt gusts on passage will feel like short-lived puffs, but shake them out of the cockpit awning and secure the trampoline gear anyway.
Overnight SSE at Panarea blows into the exposed sector of all three buoy fields; expect roll and set an anchor watch.
briefing.confidence_note: IFS, AIFS and ICON-2i agree closely on the light easterly pattern, and forecast stability over 23 snapshots shows mean wind shifts of only 0.9-1.3 kt at 12-48 h lead; the main caveat is the flagged 1.0-7.4 kt spread at 06:00 Panarea and growing direction scatter (29-38°) beyond 48 h.

verification.measures: forecast stability, not verified accuracy - the reference is the newest model run for the same hour, not an observation
